newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-RP-Rorer says Sanofi not best fit.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-RP-Rorer says Sanofi not best fit.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc, a rumored suitor for Sanofi, said the French pharmaceutical and beauty products company might not be a perfect combination because of geography.

Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Chief Financial Officer Patrick Langlois also said in an interview with Reuters that the company's key priorities at the moment are to focus on innovation and the launch of new products. He made the statement in response to a question on the company's interest in mergers.
"We are in a period of farming and not in a period of hunting," Langlois said.

"Even if Sanofi is a good pharmaceutical company, it might not be a perfect fit because of the geography of its business," said Langlois. Sanofi is majority owned by Elf Aquitaine, which has indicated it would consider a merger for Sanofi to boost profitability.
Rhone-Poulenc Rorer, 68-percent owned by France-based Rhone-Poulenc SA, is based in Collegeville, Pennsylvania, while Sanofi is based in France.

Oil group Elf Aquitaine holds about 53 percent of Sanofi stock. In December, it said it would not insist on keeping its majority stake in Sanofi but would remain an important shareholder in the company.

"It would be desirable for Sanofi to move nearer other pharmaceuticals laboratories through a merger, in order to speed up its development and increase its profitability," Elf said in a statement in December.
Analysts said then a merger with Rhone-Poulenc Rorer would be a favorite candidate.
